what_it_measured.text: Differential Effects of Oxytocin Receptor Antagonists, Atosiban and Nolasiban, on Oxytocin Receptor–Mediated Signaling in Human Amnion and Myometrium

dose.text: Prelabor amnion epithelial cells were stimulated for 5 minutes, 15 minutes, 30 minutes, 2 hours, 4 hours, and 6 hours with atosiban (10 μM) and/or OT (10 nM). (A and B) Representative Western blots for the phosphorylated NF-κB p65 subunit, ERK1/2, and p38 MAPK (A), as well as COX-2 and p-cPLA2 (B), are shown above their corresponding densitometry graphs with fold changes compared with NS controls.

endpoint.text: Consistent with the activation of these inflammatory mediators, OT led to increases in the expression of cyclooxygenase-2 and phosphorylated cytosolic phospholipase A2, which was reflected in prostaglandin E2 synthesis.

reported_results.text: (B and C) Densitometric analyses showed significant decreases in OT-mediated expression of COX-2 (B) and p-cPLA2 (C) in the presence of nolasiban (n = 6; ***P , 0.001 versus NS; #P , 0.05; ##P , 0.01; ###P , 0.001 versus OT-treated samples; ANOVA).

The PGE2 enzyme-linked immunosorbent assay demonstrated a significant inhibition of OT-mediated PGE2 production by nolasiban (n = 6; *P , 0.05; ***P , 0.001 versus NS; ###P , 0.001 versus OT-treated samples; ANOVA).
Matched β-actin loading controls confirm equal loading (n = 6; *P < 0.05; **P < 0.01; ***P < 0.001 compared with NS; ANOVA).

(A and B) Representative Western blots for the phosphorylated NF-κB p65 subunit, ERK1/2, and p38 MAPK (A), as well as COX-2 and p-cPLA2 (B), are shown above their corresponding densitometry graphs with fold changes compared with nonstimulated controls.

The OTR antagonist (nolasiban) alone had no significant effect on the OT-induced activation of NF-κB and MAPKs, and the presence of nolasiban blocked the effects of OT on NF-κB and p38 kinase, reaching significance at the 10-μM dose (P < 0.01; Fig. 10).
